gloss: to make a habit of; to habituate; to train oneself to do

definitions.gloss: to make a habit of; to habituate; to train (someone/oneself) to do something regularly
definitions.explanation: To deliberately establish a behavior as a regular routine, either for oneself or for someone else, through repeated practice.

examples.japanese: {早起|はやお}きを{習慣付|しゅうかんづ}ける。
examples.english: To make a habit of waking up early.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもに{手洗|てあら}いを{習慣付|しゅうかんづ}けた。
examples.english: I trained my child to make hand washing a habit.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}{少|すこ}しずつでも{運動|うんどう}を{習慣付|しゅうかんづ}けることが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It is important to make a habit of exercising a little every day.

notes:
A compound verb from {習慣|しゅうかん} (habit, custom) and {付|づ}ける (to attach, to apply). Means to establish something as a regular habit, either for oneself or for others. Often used in contexts of child-rearing, health, and self-improvement.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {早起|はやお}きを{習慣付|しゅうかんづ}ける: to make early rising a habit
- {運動|うんどう}を{習慣付|しゅうかんづ}ける: to make exercise a habit
- {読書|どくしょ}を{習慣付|しゅうかんづ}ける: to make reading a habit
- {子|こ}どもに{習慣付|しゅうかんづ}ける: to instill a habit in children

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {身|み}に{付|つ}ける: to acquire (a skill, habit) — broader; not limited to habits
- {慣|な}れる: to get used to — passive process of becoming accustomed rather than deliberate habit formation
- {癖|くせ}にする: to make into a habit — more colloquial; can be positive or negative
